profile_text.body:
NVIDIA Research is the research arm of NVIDIA, based in Santa Clara, CA, USA. On its own site the lab describes itself as focused on developing technology and finding breakthroughs, with work spanning generative AI, graphics, and related areas. It offers an AI Playground where visitors can try demos from its research teams, and it points to open-source resources intended to simplify programming tasks for AI researchers, including NVIDIA Sionna, Kaolin, Kaolin Wisp, Imaginaire, and CUDA-X.

The site also describes NVIDIA AI Foundation Models, which it presents as an easy-to-use interface for trying curated and optimized AI models directly from a browser, running on the NVIDIA accelerated computing stack. Kaolin is described as a PyTorch library that accelerates 3D deep learning research through differentiable 3D modules, with a model zoo of 3D deep learning architectures. CUDA is described as a parallel computing platform and programming model developed by NVIDIA for general computing on GPUs, and CUDA-X as a collection of libraries for AI and high-performance computing built on top of CUDA.

The record also lists a law exposure count of 281 in California. No products, lawsuits, or MCP servers are recorded for the lab.
